- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days.
- Model overestimates prices after sharp spikes (e.g., 76+), often overshooting by 2–5% and failing to correct quickly.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: after a spike, it incorrectly assumes price will fall further than it actually does, then later overcorrects.
- Forecast lags behind true price movements by 1–3 days, particularly in the first 7–10 days of the forecast window.
- Model tends to underestimate the magnitude of price recovery after a dip, especially in the 15–20 day range.
- Model overconfident in short-term volatility, leading to overestimation of price swings in the first 5 days.
- Model fails to capture the “rebound” effect after a sharp drop — it underestimates the price rebound and overestimates the continuation of the decline.
- Model shows persistent bias toward lower prices in the last 5–7 days of the forecast, even when true prices are rising.
